card.name: French Cancan
card.tagline: High-kicking Parisian music-hall dance of the Moulin Rouge.
card.profile: The can-can (cancan) is a high-energy music-hall dance that emerged in working-class Parisian dance halls; per Britannica it was popular in Parisian dance halls in the 1830s and appeared in variety shows and revues from the 1840s, in lively 2/4 time danced at first to quadrille or galop music. It evolved from the final figure of the quadrille and the galop. Signature moves are the high kick (battement), rond de jambe, port d'armes, cartwheel and grand ecart (jump splits), with vigorous skirt-and-petticoat work. Choreographer Pierre Sandrini formalized the staged 'French Cancan' at the Moulin Rouge in the 1920s and his Bal Tabarin from 1928 (Wikipedia; Britannica).
card.insight: The tune most associated with it is Offenbach's 'Infernal Galop' (1858, from 'Orphee aux Enfers'); per Wikipedia it was never officially banned, despite the legend (Wikipedia).
